section-227-1.TO: appoint— (a) the Investigatory Powers Commissioner, and (b) such number of other Judicial Commissioners as the Prime Minister considers necessary for the carrying out of the functions of the Judicial Commissioners

section-227-10A.FOR: a further appeal, or request for a further review
section-227-10A.TO: be made to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner
section-227-10A.IN RELATION TO: the decision of the Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioner
section-227-10A.WHERE: — (a) the exercise of a function of the Investigatory Powers Commissioner mentioned in subsection (8A)(d) is delegated to a Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioner in accordance with subsection (8)(a), and (b) the Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioner decides the appeal or review (and any action to take as a result)

section-227-6.TO: have regard to a memorandum of understanding agreed between the Prime Minister and the Scottish Ministers

section-227-6A.TO: appoint up to two persons who are Judicial Commissioners to be Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioners

section-227-8.TO: delegate the exercise of functions of the Investigatory Powers Commissioner to— (a) a Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioner, or (b) any other Judicial Commissioner
section-227-8.TO_2: such extent as the Investigatory Powers Commissioner may decide

section-227-8D.TO: delegate to one Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioner the exercise of the function of the Investigatory Powers Commissioner of deciding— (a) an appeal against, or a review of, a decision made by the other Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioner, and (b) any action to take as a result
section-227-8D.WHERE: there are two Deputy Investigatory Powers Commissioners

section-228-2.TO: be appointed for a term of three years

section-228-3.FOR: a person who ceases to be a Judicial Commissioner (otherwise than under subsection (5))

section-228-4.BEFORE: the end of the term for which the Commissioner is appointed
section-228-4.UNLESS: a resolution approving the removal has been passed by each House of Parliament

section-228-5.TO: remove a Judicial Commissioner from office
section-228-5.IF: — (a) a bankruptcy order is made against the Commissioner or the Commissioner's estate is sequestrated or the Commissioner makes a composition or arrangement with, or grants a trust deed for, the Commissioner's creditors, (b) any of the following orders is made against the Commissioner— (i) a disqualification order under the Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986 or the Company Directors Disqualification (Northern Ireland) Order 2002, (ii) an order under section 429(2)(b) of the Insolvency Act 1986 (failure to pay under county court administration order), (iii) an order under section 429(2) of the Insolvency Act 1986 (disabilities on revocation of county court administration order), (c) the Commissioner's disqualification undertaking is accepted under section 7 or 8 of the Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986 or under the Company Directors Disqualification (Northern Ireland) Order 2002, or (d) the Commissioner is convicted in the United Kingdom, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man of an offence and receives a sentence of imprisonment (whether suspended or not)

section-228A-2.TO: appoint one or more persons to carry out Judicial Commissioner functions

section-228A-4.TO: be appointed under subsection (2) for one or more terms not exceeding six months each and not exceeding three years in total

section-228A-5.TO: notify the following persons of the appointment— (a) the Prime Minister; (b) the Secretary of State; (c) the Scottish Ministers; (d) the Lord Chancellor; (e) the Lord Chief Justice of England and Wales; (f) the Lord President of the Court of Session; (g) the Lord Chief Justice of Northern Ireland
section-228A-5.AFTER: the appointment of any temporary Judicial Commissioner

section-229-1.TO: keep under review (including by way of audit, inspection and investigation) the exercise by public authorities of statutory functions relating to— (a) the interception of communications, (b) the acquisition or retention of communications data, (c) the acquisition of secondary data or related systems data under Chapter 1 of Part 2 or Chapter 1 of Part 6, or (d) equipment interference

section-229-3.TO: keep under review (including by way of audit, inspection and investigation)— (a) the acquisition, retention, use or disclosure of bulk personal datasets by an intelligence service, (b) the giving and operation of notices under section 252 (national security notices), (d) the exercise of functions by virtue of sections 1 to 4 of the Prisons (Interference with Wireless Telegraphy) Act 2012, (e) the exercise of functions by virtue of Part 2 or 3 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 (surveillance, covert human intelligence sources and investigation of electronic data protected by encryption etc.) , (f) the adequacy of the arrangements by virtue of which the duties imposed by section 55 of that Act are sought to be discharged, (g) the exercise of functions by virtue of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers (Scotland) Act 2000 (2000 asp 11) (surveillance and covert human intelligence sources), (h) the exercise of functions under Part 3 of the Police Act 1997 (authorisation of action in respect of property), (i) the exercise by the Secretary of State of functions under sections 5 to 7 of the Intelligence Services Act 1994 (warrants for interference with wireless telegraphy, entry and interference with property etc.) , and (j) the exercise by the Scottish Ministers (by virtue of provision made under section 63 of the Scotland Act 1998) of functions under sections 5 and 6(3) and (4) of the Act of 1994

section-229-3A.TO: keep under review the compliance by public authorities with the terms of the Agreement between the Government of the United Kingdom and the Government of the United States of America on access to electronic data for the purpose of countering serious crime dated 3rd October 2019

section-229-3B.TO: keep under review (including by way of audit, inspection and investigation) the process operated by GCHQ for determining whether information about vulnerabilities in technology should be disclosed

section-229-3C.TO: keep under review (including by way of audit, inspection and investigation) compliance by the persons mentioned in subsection (3D) with 'The Principles Relating to the Detention and Interviewing of Detainees Overseas and the Passing and Receipt of Intelligence Relating to Detainees', as published on 18th July 2019

section-229-3E.TO: keep under review (including by way of audit, inspection and investigation) compliance by any part of His Majesty’s forces, or by any part of the Ministry of Defence, with policies governing— (a) the use of surveillance outside the United Kingdom, and (b) the use and conduct of covert human intelligence sources outside the United Kingdom, (whether or not authorised under the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000)

section-229-4A.TO: keep under review the exercise of the power to grant or renew authorisations under section 29B of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000
section-229-4A.IN: keeping matters under review in accordance with subsection (3)(e)

section-229-4B.TO: keep under review whether public authorities are complying with any requirements imposed on them by virtue of Part 2 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 in relation to juvenile criminal conduct authorisations and vulnerable adult criminal conduct authorisations
section-229-4B.IN: keeping under review the exercise of the power mentioned in subsection (4A)

section-229-5.TO: keep under review the operation of safeguards to protect privacy
section-229-5.IN: keeping matters under review in accordance with this section

section-229-6.TO: act in a way which the Commissioner considers to be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to— (a) national security, (b) the prevention or detection of serious crime, or (c) the economic well-being of the United Kingdom

section-229-7.TO: ensure that the Commissioner does not— (a) jeopardise the success of an intelligence or security operation or a law enforcement operation, (b) compromise the safety or security of those involved, or (c) unduly impede the operational effectiveness of an intelligence service, a police force, a government department or Her Majesty's forces

section-230-1.TO: keep under review the carrying out of any aspect of the functions of— (a) an intelligence service, (b) a head of an intelligence service, (c) any part of Her Majesty's forces, or of the Ministry of Defence, so far as engaging in intelligence activities, or (d) any public authority not mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (c), or any part of such an authority, so far as engaging in intelligence activities
section-230-1.SO FAR AS: directed to do so by the Prime Minister

section-230-3.TO: give a direction under this section
section-230-3.AT: the request of the Investigatory Powers Commissioner or the Intelligence and Security Committee of Parliament or otherwise

section-230-4.TO: publish, in a manner which the Prime Minister considers appropriate, any direction under this section (and any revocation of such a direction)
section-230-4.EXCEPT SO FAR AS: it appears to the Prime Minister that such publication would be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to— (a) national security, (b) the prevention or detection of serious crime, (c) the economic well-being of the United Kingdom, or (d) the continued discharge of the functions of any public authority whose activities include activities that are subject to review by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner

section-231-1.TO: inform a person of any relevant error relating to that person of which the Commissioner is aware
section-231-1.IF: the Commissioner considers that— (a) the error is a serious error, and (b) it is in the public interest for the person to be informed of the error

section-231-2.TO: decide that an error is a serious error
section-231-2.UNLESS: the Commissioner considers that the error has caused significant prejudice or harm to the person concerned

section-231-4.TO: consider— (a) the seriousness of the error and its effect on the person concerned, and (b) the extent to which disclosing the error would be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to— (i) national security, (ii) the prevention or detection of serious crime, (iii) the economic well-being of the United Kingdom, or (iv) the continued discharge of the functions of any of the intelligence services

section-231-5.TO: ask the public authority which has made the error to make submissions to the Commissioner about the matters concerned
section-231-5.BEFORE: making a decision under subsection (1)(a) or (b)

section-231-6.TO: — (a) inform the person of any rights that the person may have to apply to the Investigatory Powers Tribunal, and (b) provide such details of the error as the Commissioner considers to be necessary for the exercise of those rights, having regard in particular to the extent to which disclosing the details would be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to anything falling within subsection (4)(b)(i) to (iv)
section-231-6.WHEN: informing a person under subsection (1) of an error

section-231-7.TO: inform the person to whom it relates of a relevant error

section-231-8.TO: include information about— (a) the number of relevant errors of which the Investigatory Powers Commissioner has become aware during the year to which the report relates, (b) the number of relevant errors which the Commissioner has decided during that year were serious errors, and (c) the number of persons informed under subsection (1) during that year

section-232-1.TO: give the Investigatory Powers Tribunal all such documents, information and other assistance (including the Commissioner's opinion as to any issue falling to be determined by the Tribunal) as the Tribunal may require— (a) in connection with the investigation of any matter by the Tribunal, or (b) otherwise for the purposes of the Tribunal's consideration or determination of any matter

section-232-2.TO: provide advice or information to any public authority or other person
section-232-2.IN RELATION TO: matters for which a Judicial Commissioner is responsible

section-232-3.BEFORE: providing any advice or information under subsection (2)
section-232-3.IF: it appears to the Commissioner that providing the advice or information might be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to— (a) national security, (b) the prevention or detection of serious crime, (c) the economic well-being of the United Kingdom, or (d) the continued discharge of the functions of any public authority whose activities include activities that are subject to review by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner

section-232-4.TO: In addition to consulting the Secretary of State under subsection (3), consult the Scottish Ministers
section-232-4.IF: it appears to the Commissioner that providing the advice or information might be prejudicial to— (a) the prevention or detection of serious crime by a Scottish public authority, or (b) the continued discharge of any devolved functions of a Scottish public authority whose activities include activities that are subject to review by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner

section-234-1.TO: make a report to the Prime Minister about the carrying out of the functions of the Judicial Commissioners
section-234-1.AFTER: the end of each calendar year

section-234-2.TO: include— (a) statistics on the use of the investigatory powers which are subject to review by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner (including the number of warrants or authorisations issued, given, considered or approved during the year), (b) information about the results of such use (including its impact), (ba) information about the use of the power to grant or renew authorisations under section 29B of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000, (c) information about the operation of the safeguards conferred by this Act in relation to items subject to legal privilege, confidential journalistic material and sources of journalistic information, (d) information about the following kinds of warrants issued, considered or approved during the year— (i) targeted interception warrants or targeted examination warrants of the kind referred to in section 17(2), (ii) targeted equipment interference warrants relating to matters within paragraph (b), (c), (e), (f), (g) or (h) of section 101(1), and (iii) targeted examination warrants under Part 5 relating to matters within any of paragraphs (b) to (e) of section 101(2), (e) information about the operational purposes specified during the year in warrants issued under Part 6 or 7, (f) the information on errors required by virtue of section 231(8), (g) information about the work of the Technology Advisory Panel, (h) information about the funding, staffing and other resources of the Judicial Commissioners, and (i) details of public engagements undertaken by the Judicial Commissioners or their staff

section-234-3.TO: make any report to the Prime Minister which has been requested by the Prime Minister

section-234-4.TO: make any such report to the Prime Minister, on any matter relating to the functions of the Judicial Commissioners, as the Investigatory Powers Commissioner considers appropriate

section-234-5.TO: include such recommendations as the Investigatory Powers Commissioner considers appropriate about any matter relating to the functions of the Judicial Commissioners

section-234-6.TO: — (a) publish the report, and (b) lay a copy of the published report before Parliament together with a statement as to whether any part of the report has been excluded from publication under subsection (7)
section-234-6.ON: receiving a report from the Investigatory Powers Commissioner under subsection (1)

section-234-7.TO: exclude from publication any part of a report under subsection (1)
section-234-7.AFTER: consultation with the Investigatory Powers Commissioner and (so far as the report relates to functions under Part 3 of the Police Act 1997) the Scottish Ministers
section-234-7.IF: in the opinion of the Prime Minister, the publication of that part would be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to— (a) national security, (b) the prevention or detection of serious crime, (c) the economic well-being of the United Kingdom, or (d) the continued discharge of the functions of any public authority whose activities include activities that are subject to review by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner

section-234-8.TO: send a copy of every report and statement as laid before Parliament under subsection (6)(b) to the Scottish Ministers
lay the copy report and statement before the Scottish Parliament

section-234-9.TO: publish any report under subsection (3) or (4), or any part of such a report
section-234-9.IF: requested to do so by the Prime Minister

section-234-11.TO: send to the Intelligence and Security Committee of Parliament a copy of the report
section-234-11.SO FAR AS: it relates to— (a) the investigation, inspection or audit concerned, and (b) the functions of the Committee falling within section 2 of the Justice and Security Act 2013

section-235-1.TO: carry out such investigations, inspections and audits as the Commissioner considers appropriate for the purposes of the Commissioner's functions

section-235-2.TO: disclose or provide to a Judicial Commissioner all such documents and information as the Commissioner may require for the purposes of the Commissioner's functions

section-235-3.TO: provide a Judicial Commissioner with such assistance as the Commissioner may require in carrying out any investigation, inspection or audit for the purposes of the Commissioner's functions

section-235-4.TO: include such access to apparatus, systems or other facilities or services as the Judicial Commissioner concerned may require in carrying out any investigation, inspection or audit for the purposes of the Commissioner's functions

section-235-5.TO: report to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner any refusal by a telecommunications operator or postal operator to comply with any requirements imposed by virtue of this Act

section-235-6.FOR: A public authority, telecommunications operator or postal operator
section-235-6.TO: report to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner any relevant error (within the meaning given by section 231(9)) of which it is aware

section-235A-2.TO: report the personal data breach to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner

section-235A-3.TO: disclose information about a personal data breach to the Information Commissioner
section-235A-3.WHERE: a telecommunications operator reports the breach to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner under subsection (2)

section-235A-4.TO: consider whether the breach is serious
section-235A-4.WHERE: a Judicial Commissioner discloses information about a personal data breach to the Information Commissioner under subsection (3)
a Judicial Commissioner discloses information about a personal data breach to the Information Commissioner under subsection (3)
section-235A-4.IF: the Information Commissioner considers that the breach is serious

section-235A-5.TO: inform an individual of any personal data breach relating to that individual of which the Commissioner is notified under subsection (4) (b)
section-235A-5.IF: the Commissioner considers that it is in the public interest for the individual to be informed of the breach

section-235A-6.TO: consider— (a) the seriousness of the breach and its effect on the individual concerned, and (b) the extent to which disclosing the breach would be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to— (i) national security, (ii) the prevention or detection of serious crime, (iii) the economic well-being of the United Kingdom, or (iv) the continued discharge of the functions of any of the intelligence services

section-235A-7.TO: ask— (a) the Secretary of State, and (b) any public authority that the Investigatory Powers Commissioner considers appropriate, to make submissions to the Commissioner about the matters concerned

section-235A-8.TO: — (a) inform the individual of any rights that the individual may have to apply to the Investigatory Powers Tribunal in relation to the breach, and (b) provide such details of the breach as the Commissioner considers to be necessary for the exercise of those rights, having regard in particular to the extent to which disclosing the details would be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to anything falling within subsection (6) (b) (i) to (iv)
section-235A-8.WHEN: informing an individual under subsection (5) of a breach

section-235A-9.TO: inform the individual to whom it relates of a personal data breach notified to the Commissioner under subsection (4)(b)

section-236-2.TO: inform the Intelligence and Security Committee of Parliament of the Commissioner's decision as to whether to carry out the investigation, inspection or audit

section-238-2.TO: provide the Judicial Commissioners with— (a) such staff, and (b) such accommodation, equipment and other facilities and services, as the Secretary of State considers necessary for the carrying out of the Commissioners' functions
section-238-2.AFTER: consultation with the Investigatory Powers Commissioner
section-238-2.SUBJECT TO: the approval of the Treasury as to numbers of staff

section-238-3.TO: pay to the Judicial Commissioners such allowances as the Scottish Ministers consider appropriate in respect of the exercise by the Commissioners of functions which relate to the exercise by Scottish public authorities of devolved functions

section-238-5.FOR: The Investigatory Powers Commissioner or any other Judicial Commissioner
section-238-5.TO: delegate the exercise of functions of that Commissioner to any member of staff of the Judicial Commissioners or any other person acting on behalf of the Commissioners

section-239-1.TO: by regulations modify the functions of the Investigatory Powers Commissioner or any other Judicial Commissioner

section-239-2.TO: modify any function conferred by virtue of this Act on a Judicial Commissioner to approve, quash or cancel— (a) an authorisation or warrant, or (b) the variation or renewal of an authorisation or warrant

section-239-3.FOR: The power to make regulations under this section (including that power as extended by section 267(1)(c))
section-239-3.TO: be exercised by modifying any provision made by or under an enactment (including this Act)

section-240-3.TO: by regulations provide for the abolition of the office of the Investigatory Powers Commissioner for Northern Ireland
section-240-3.WITH: the consent of the Northern Ireland Assembly

section-240-4.FOR: The power to make regulations under subsection (3) (including that power as extended by section 267(1)(c))
section-240-4.TO: be exercised by modifying any provision made by or under an enactment (including this Act)

section-240-5.FOR: Regulations made by virtue of subsection (4)
section-240-5.TO: repeal— (a) section 61 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 (the Investigatory Powers Commissioner for Northern Ireland), and (b) the words “or the Investigatory Powers Commissioner for Northern Ireland” in section 229(4)(f) of this Act

section-245-2.FOR: The regulations providing for the membership of the Technical Advisory Board
section-245-2.TO: make provision which is calculated to ensure— (a) that the membership of the Board includes persons likely effectively to represent the interests of persons on whom obligations may be imposed by virtue of retention notices under Part 4, national security notices under section 252 or technical capability notices under section 253, (b) that the membership of the Board includes persons likely effectively to represent the interests of persons entitled to apply for warrants under Part 2, 5, 6 or 7 or authorisations under Part 3, (c) that such other persons (if any) as the Secretary of State considers appropriate may be appointed to be members of the Board, and (d) that the Board is so constituted as to produce a balance between the representation of the interests mentioned in paragraph (a) and the representation of those mentioned in paragraph (b)

section-245-3.TO: make provision about quorum and the filling of vacancies

section-246-1.TO: ensure that there is a Technology Advisory Panel to provide advice to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner, the Secretary of State and the Scottish Ministers about— (a) the impact of changing technology on the exercise of investigatory powers whose exercise is subject to review by the Commissioner, and (b) the availability and development of techniques to use such powers while minimising interference with privacy

section-246-2.TO: provide advice to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner about such matters falling within subsection (1)(a) or (b) as the Commissioner may direct

section-246-3.TO: provide advice to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner about such matters falling within subsection (1)(a) or (b) as it considers appropriate (whether or not requested to do so)

section-246-4.TO: provide advice to the Secretary of State or the Scottish Ministers about such matters falling within subsection (1)(a) or (b) as it considers appropriate (whether or not requested to do so)

section-246-4.FOR: such advice to the Scottish Ministers
section-246-4.TO: only relate to matters for which the Scottish Ministers are responsible

section-246-5.TO: make a report to the Investigatory Powers Commissioner about the carrying out of the functions of the Panel
section-246-5.AFTER: the end of each calendar year

section-246-6.TO: send a copy of the report to the Secretary of State and (so far as relating to matters for which the Scottish Ministers are responsible) the Scottish Ministers

section-247-1.TO: appoint such number of persons as members of the Technology Advisory Panel as the Commissioner considers necessary for the carrying out of the functions of the Panel

section-247-3.TO: act in a way which the member considers to be contrary to the public interest or prejudicial to— (a) national security, (b) the prevention or detection of serious crime, or (c) the economic well-being of the United Kingdom

section-247-4.TO: ensure that the member does not— (a) jeopardise the success of an intelligence or security operation or a law enforcement operation, (b) compromise the safety or security of those involved, or (c) unduly impede the operational effectiveness of an intelligence service, a police force, a government department or Her Majesty's forces

section-249-1.TO: ensure that arrangements are in force for securing that telecommunications operators and postal operators receive an appropriate contribution in respect of such of their relevant costs as the Secretary of State considers appropriate

section-249-3.TO: provide for payment of a contribution to be subject to terms and conditions determined by the Secretary of State

section-249-4.TO: include a condition on the operator concerned to comply with any audit that may reasonably be required to monitor the claim for costs

section-249-5.TO: provide for the Secretary of State to determine— (a) the scope and extent of the arrangements, and (b) the appropriate level of contribution which should be made in each case

section-249-6.TO: apply for different cases or descriptions of case

section-249-7.FOR: a retention notice under Part 4 given to a telecommunications operator or a postal operator, or a national security notice under section 252 given to a telecommunications operator
section-249-7.TO: specify the level or levels of contribution which the Secretary of State has determined should be made in respect of the costs incurred, or likely to be incurred, by the operator as a result of the notice in complying with that Part or (as the case may be) with the national security notice

section-249-8.TO: For the purpose of complying with this section, make, or arrange for the making of, payments out of money provided by Parliament

section-250-1.TO: — (a) develop, provide, maintain or improve, or (b) enter into financial or other arrangements with any person for the development, provision, maintenance or improvement of, such apparatus, systems or other facilities or services as the Secretary of State considers appropriate for enabling or otherwise facilitating compliance by the Secretary of State, another public authority or any other person with this Act

section-250-2.TO: include arrangements consisting of the giving of financial assistance by the Secretary of State

section-250-3.TO: be given by way of— (i) grant, (ii) loan, (iii) guarantee or indemnity, (iv) investment, or (v) incurring expenditure for the benefit of the person assisted

section-250-3.SUBJECT TO: terms and conditions determined by the Secretary of State

section-250-4.FOR: Terms and conditions imposed by virtue of subsection (3)(b)
section-250-4.TO: include terms and conditions as to repayment with or without interest

section-252-1.TO: give any telecommunications operator in the United Kingdom a national security notice under this section
section-252-1.IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the notice is necessary in the interests of national security, (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct required by the notice is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, and (c) the decision to give the notice has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-252-3.TO: require the operator to whom it is given— (a) to carry out any conduct, including the provision of services or facilities, for the purpose of— (i) facilitating anything done by an intelligence service under any enactment other than this Act, or (ii) dealing with an emergency (within the meaning of Part 1 of the Civil Contingencies Act 2004); (b) to provide services or facilities for the purpose of assisting an intelligence service to carry out its functions more securely or more effectively

section-252-5.TO: give any telecommunications operator a national security notice the main purpose of which is to require the operator to do something for which a warrant or authorisation under a relevant enactment is required

section-252-7.TO: specify such period as appears to the Secretary of State to be reasonable as the period within which the steps specified in the notice are to be taken

section-252-8.FOR: Conduct required by a national security notice
section-252-8.TO: be treated as lawful for all purposes
section-252-8.TO THE EXTENT THAT: it would not otherwise be so treated

section-253-1.TO: give a relevant operator a technical capability notice under this section
section-253-1.IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the notice is necessary for securing that the operator or another relevant operator has the capability to provide any assistance which such operator may be required to provide in relation to any relevant authorisation, (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct required by the notice is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, and (c) the decision to give the notice has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-253-4.TO: specify an obligation that may be imposed on any relevant operators
section-253-4.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State considers it is reasonable to do so for the purpose of securing— (a) that it is (and remains) practicable to impose requirements on those relevant operators to provide assistance in relation to relevant authorisations, and (b) that it is (and remains) practicable for those relevant operators to comply with those requirements

section-253-6.TO: consult the following persons— (a) the Technical Advisory Board, (b) persons appearing to the Secretary of State to be likely to be subject to any obligations specified in the regulations, (c) persons representing persons falling within paragraph (b), and (d) persons with statutory functions in relation to persons falling within that paragraph
section-253-6.BEFORE: making any regulations under this section

section-253-7.TO: specify such period as appears to the Secretary of State to be reasonable as the period within which the steps specified in the notice are to be taken
specify different periods in relation to different steps

section-253-8.TO: be given to persons outside the United Kingdom
require things to be done, or not to be done, outside the United Kingdom

section-254-2.TO: review the Secretary of State's conclusions as to the following matters— (a) whether the notice is necessary as mentioned in section 252(1)(a) or (as the case may be) section 253(1)(a), and (b) whether the conduct that would be required by the notice is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct
section-254-2.IN: deciding whether to approve a decision to give a relevant notice

section-254-3.TO: — (a) apply the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review, and (b) consider the matters referred to in subsection (2) with a sufficient degree of care as to ensure that the Judicial Commissioner complies with the duties imposed by section 2 (general duties in relation to privacy)

section-254-4.TO: give the Secretary of State written reasons for the refusal
section-254-4.WHERE: the Judicial Commissioner refuses to approve a decision to give a relevant notice

section-254-5.TO: ask the Investigatory Powers Commissioner to decide whether to approve the decision to give the notice
section-254-5.WHERE: a Judicial Commissioner, other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner, refuses to approve a decision to give a relevant notice

section-255-2.BEFORE: giving a relevant notice to that person

section-255-3.TO: take into account— (a) the likely benefits of the notice, (b) the likely number of users (if known) of any postal or telecommunications service to which the notice relates, (c) the technical feasibility of complying with the notice, (d) the likely cost of complying with the notice, and (e) any other effect of the notice on the person (or description of person) to whom it relates

section-255-4.TO: take into account the technical feasibility, and likely cost, of complying with any obligations relating to the removal by a person of electronic protection applied by or on behalf of that person to any communications or data
section-255-4.IN THE CASE OF: a technical capability notice that would impose those obligations

section-255-6.TO: be given to a person outside the United Kingdom in any of the following ways (as well as by electronic or other means of giving a notice)— (a) by delivering it to the person's principal office within the United Kingdom or, if the person has no such office in the United Kingdom, to any place in the United Kingdom where the person carries on business or conducts activities; (b) if the person has specified an address in the United Kingdom as one at which the person, or someone on the person's behalf, will accept documents of the same description as a notice, by delivering it to that address

section-255-7.TO: by regulations make further provision about the giving of relevant notices

section-255-8.FOR: A person to whom a relevant notice is given, or any person employed or engaged for the purposes of that person's business
section-255-8.TO: disclose the existence or contents of the notice to any other person without the permission of the Secretary of State

section-255-9.FOR: a person to whom a relevant notice is given

section-256-2.TO: keep each relevant notice under review

section-256-3.TO: — (a) vary a relevant notice; (b) revoke a relevant notice (whether wholly or in part)

section-256-4.TO: vary a national security notice given to a person
section-256-4.ONLY IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the variation is necessary in the interests of national security, (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct required by the notice as varied is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, and (c) if the variation would impose further requirements on the person, the decision to vary the notice has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner (but see subsection (6))

section-256-5.TO: vary a technical capability notice given to a person
section-256-5.ONLY IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the variation is necessary for securing that the person has the capability to provide any assistance which the person may be required to provide in relation to any relevant authorisation (within the meaning of section 253), (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct required by the notice as varied is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct, and (c) if the variation would impose further requirements on the person, the decision to vary the notice has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner (but see subsection (6))

section-256-7.TO: give notice of the variation or revocation to any person
section-256-7.IF: the Secretary of State varies or revokes a relevant notice given to that person

section-256A-1.TO: be renewed by a notice given by the Secretary of State
section-256A-1.AT: any time during the renewal period

section-256A-5.TO: give notice in writing of the renewal
section-256A-5.IF: the Secretary of State renews a relevant notice given to any person

section-257-3A.TO: make any relevant changes to telecommunications or postal services, or telecommunication systems, to which obligations imposed by the notice given under section 252 or 253 relate
section-257-3A.WHERE: this subsection applies to the person

section-257-4.TO: review any notice so far as referred to the Secretary of State under subsection (1) (and accordingly decide what action to take under subsection (9))
section-257-4.BEFORE: the end of the review period

section-257-5.TO: consult— (a) the Technical Advisory Board, and (b) a Judicial Commissioner

section-257-6.TO: consider the technical requirements and the financial consequences, for the person who has made the reference, of the notice so far as referred

section-257-7.TO: consider whether the notice so far as referred is proportionate

section-257-8.TO: — (a) give the person concerned and the Secretary of State the opportunity to provide evidence, or make representations, to them before reaching their conclusions, and (b) report their conclusions to— (i) the person, and (ii) the Secretary of State

section-257-8A.TO: give a direction to the person concerned or the Secretary of State specifying the period within which the person or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) may provide evidence, or make representations, in accordance with subsection (8)(a)

section-257-9.TO: decide whether to — (a) vary or revoke the notice under section 256, or (b) give a notice under this section to the person confirming its effect
section-257-9.AFTER: considering the conclusions of the Board and the Commissioner
section-257-9.BEFORE: the end of the relevant period

section-257-10.TO: vary the notice, or give a notice under subsection (9)(b) confirming its effect
section-257-10.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State's decision to do so has been approved by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner

section-257-13.TO: include provision enabling any period provided for by the regulations to be extended by the Secretary of State where the extension is agreed by the Secretary of State, the person concerned and a Judicial Commissioner

section-257-14.TO: include provision enabling any period provided for by the regulations to be extended by the Secretary of State
section-257-14.WHERE: the Secretary of State considers that there are exceptional circumstances that justify the extension

section-257-14.TO: include provision enabling any period provided for by the regulations to be extended by the Secretary of State
section-257-14.IN: any other circumstances specified in the regulations

section-258-2.TO: review the Secretary of State's conclusions as to the following matters— (a) whether the relevant notice as varied or confirmed is necessary as mentioned in section 252(1)(a) or (as the case may be) section 253(1)(a), and (b) whether the conduct required by the relevant notice, as varied or confirmed, is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct
section-258-2.IN: deciding whether to approve a decision to vary a relevant notice as mentioned in section 257(9)(a), or to give a notice under section 257(9)(b) confirming the effect of a relevant notice

section-258-3.TO: — (a) apply the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review, and (b) consider the matters referred to in subsection (2) with a sufficient degree of care as to ensure that the Investigatory Powers Commissioner complies with the duties imposed by section 2 (general duties in relation to privacy)

section-258-4.TO: give the Secretary of State written reasons for the refusal
section-258-4.WHERE: the Investigatory Powers Commissioner refuses to approve a decision to vary a relevant notice as mentioned in section 257(9)(a), or to give a notice under section 257(9)(b) confirming the effect of a relevant notice

section-258A-1.TO: give a relevant operator a notice in writing under this section requiring the operator to notify the Secretary of State of any proposals of the operator to make any relevant changes specified in the notice

section-258A-4.TO: specify changes by reference to the impact of the changes on the capability of a relevant operator to provide any assistance which the operator may be required to provide in relation to any warrant, authorisation or notice issued or given under this Act

section-258A-5.TO: give a relevant operator a notice under this section
section-258A-5.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State considers that— (a) the notice is necessary for maintaining the capability of the relevant operator to provide any assistance which the operator may be required to provide in relation to any warrant, authorisation or notice issued or given under this Act, and (b) the conduct required by the notice is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct

section-258A-6.TO: take into account— (a) the likely benefits of the notice, (b) the likely number of users (if known) of any postal or telecommunications service to which the notice relates, (c) the likely cost of complying with the notice, and (d) any other effect of the notice on the operator to whom it relates
section-258A-6.BEFORE: giving a notice under this section

section-258A-7.BEFORE: giving a notice under this section to that operator

section-258A-8.FOR: A relevant operator to whom a notice is given under this section, or any person employed or engaged for the purposes of that relevant operator’s business
section-258A-8.TO: disclose the existence or contents of the notice to any other person without the permission of the Secretary of State

section-258A-9.FOR: A relevant operator to whom a notice is given under this section
section-258A-9.A: reasonable time before making any relevant changes to which the notice relates

section-258B-2.TO: — (a) vary a relevant notice; (b) revoke a relevant notice (whether wholly or in part)

section-258B-3.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State considers that— (a) the variation is necessary for maintaining the capability of the relevant operator to provide any assistance which the operator may be required to provide in relation to any warrant, authorisation or notice issued or given under this Act, and (b) the conduct required by the notice, as varied, is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct

section-258B-4.TO: give any relevant operator notice in writing of the variation or revocation
section-258B-4.IF: the Secretary of State varies or revokes a relevant notice given to that relevant operator

section-260-1.TO: prepare a report on the operation of this Act
section-260-1.WITHIN: the period of 6 months beginning with the end of the initial period

section-260-3.TO: take account of any report on the operation of this Act made by a Select Committee of either House of Parliament (whether acting alone or jointly)

section-260-4.TO: — (a) publish the report prepared under subsection (1), and (b) lay a copy of it before Parliament

section-268-3.TO: lay before Parliament— (a) draft regulations, and (b) a document which explains the regulations

section-268-4.TO: make regulations in the terms of the draft regulations laid under subsection (3)
section-268-4.IF: the draft regulations are approved by a resolution of each House of Parliament

section-268-6.TO: have regard to— (a) any representations, (b) any resolution of either House of Parliament, and (c) any recommendations of a committee of either House of Parliament charged with reporting on the draft regulations, made during the 60-day period with regard to the draft regulations

section-268-7.TO: make regulations in the terms of the draft regulations
section-268-7.IF: the draft regulations are approved by a resolution of each House of Parliament

section-268-8.TO: lay before Parliament— (a) revised draft regulations, and (b) a statement giving a summary of the changes proposed
section-268-8.IF: the Secretary of State wishes to proceed with the draft regulations but with material changes

section-268-9.TO: make regulations in the terms of the revised draft regulations
section-268-9.IF: the revised draft regulations are approved by a resolution of each House of Parliament

section-270-2.TO: by regulations make such transitional, transitory or saving provision as the Secretary of State considers appropriate in connection with the coming into force of any provision of this Act

section-271-2.TO: by regulations make such provision as the Secretary of State considers appropriate in consequence of this Act

section-271-3.FOR: The power to make regulations under subsection (2)
section-271-3.TO: be exercised by modifying any provision made by or under an enactment

section-272-6.TO: by Order in Council provide for any of the provisions of this Act to extend, with or without modifications, to the Isle of Man or any of the British overseas territories

section-272-8.TO: be cited as the Investigatory Powers Act 2016
